🎉 MILESTONE PARTY TIME!!! 🎉

Countdown To 7,000,000 Minutes!

From 18th of July, 2013 at 12:30 PM NZT

Total Minutes

Progress to 7,000,000 minutes

6,000,0007,000,000

Hold Space / click / touch to rise, let go to fall. Collect amber minutes and dodge the hourglass blocks. Twist: every 4 minutes collected triggers a Time Warp: the world slows down and you’re briefly untouchable.

Hold or tap where you want to go (or use ← →) to move along the cliff. Amber markers at the top warn where a rock will fall. Grab the glowing orbs: 🛡️ Shield blocks one hit, ❄️ Slow slows the rocks, 🚀 Boost speeds you up and makes you untouchable for a few seconds.

Tap, click or press Space to drop the sliding block onto the tower. The overlap stays, the overhang falls off, and a near-perfect drop keeps the block its size and wins width back. Random speeds, and now and then a slow block. Build as high as you can!

Watch the pads light up, then repeat the pattern by tapping them (or press 1–4). You get two lives per run, the order of the colors is shuffled each time, and every pattern is new.

Hold or tap where you want to steer (or use ↑ ↓). Dodge traffic, cones and oil slicks (oil spins you out), hit boost pads, and grab coins and power-ups: 🔥 Nitro is fast and unstoppable, 🛡️ Shield blocks a crash, ⏳ Slow Time slows the world. You have three lives, and random events like rain, night and rush hour change the race.

Your dog bounces on its own: steer left and right (hold or tap, or use ← →) and the screen wraps around. Every run is a random dog with its own quirk. Watch for moving, crumbling and spring platforms, stomp the cats from above, and grab 🦴 Bone Boost, 🥏 Glide and 🏷️ Dog Tag (blocks a hit). Wind gusts and moonwalk low gravity show up now and then.

[v2.4]The Party Update: the milestone party now lasts 10 minutes with gentler confetti, a soft rainbow glow over the page, a slow zoom and its own looping music. A new Rainbow Phase cycles the page colors through the rainbow while the party runs. The party code was also checked for bugs and tidied.

[v2.3.1]Small Patch 1: the experimental golden look is gone, the real golden phase is lighter and smoother, and its pop-up text is removed. The milestone party now fires confetti from both sides of the page and no longer depends on an outside script. A batch of smaller bugs was fixed too.

[v2.3]The Mac Update: the site now works better on Macs, iPhones and iPads, with new ways to open the hidden dev menu on devices without a usable F3 key and fixes for page zoom, the on-screen keyboard and the iPhone notch. Echo Minutes plays faster, and the experimental golden look now uses the same gold as the real golden phase. A stray text bug in this log is also gone.

[v2.2.5]Mega Bug Fix PART 3: the countdown no longer shows a negative number of days on certain dates, and Doodle Dog platforms now stay within a comfortable reach of each other. Several smaller glitches were also tidied across the games and menus. A temporary experimental look for the golden phase is being tested.

[v2.2.4]Mega Bug Fix PART 2: the blue phase is now #1943ca. A few bugs are fixed, including gold text vanishing on browsers without gradient-text support. A hidden dev menu now opens at the bottom-left with Ctrl+F3, behind an access code.

[v2.2]Mega Bug Update (Part 1): every day one minigame is picked at random as the Minigame of the Day, shown with a gold outline and a star (it never repeats two days running, and it is the game you land on the first time you visit each day); every script was audited by running each game thousands of times under strict checks, which found no crashes but a few bugs that are now fixed: tapping to start Minute Racer or Doodle Dog now steers you toward where you tapped straight away, and the tick sound now also unlocks on a click or tap.

[v2.1.4]Diamond Game Update: the final two minigames, Minute Racer (a 2D race with traffic, oil slicks, boost pads, rain, night and rush-hour events and three power-ups) and Doodle Dog (a bouncing climb with a random dog each run, cats to stomp, moving, crumbling and spring platforms and three power-ups); the golden stage now glows much brighter, like a star; Mountain Climb has a richer rock face, an altitude ruler, mist and a roped climber; a faint clock tick sounds every second (never during the party, with a button to mute it); and a bug-fix pass.

[v2.1.2]MEGA UPDATE 3: two new easy minigames, Time Stack (drop sliding blocks into a tower) and Echo Minutes (repeat random light patterns); a majestic golden stage with a royal flash, shimmering gold text, drifting sparkles and a golden version label; a bigger milestone party with an opening blast, fireworks, a rainbow banner showing the milestone number and a celebratory tab title (add #party to the page link to preview it); an easier Second Hand and Mountain Climb; and a bug-fix pass.

[v2.0.6]The Power-Up Update: update names in this log are now highlighted, and Mountain Climb is a little easier (rocks fall slower, warn longer and come less often) with three twist orbs: a blue Shield that blocks one hit, a violet Slow orb that slows falling rocks, and an orange Boost that speeds you up and makes you untouchable for a few seconds, plus a bug-fix pass.

[v2.0.2]The Glow Update: every color stage now glows, starting faint and growing stronger the closer the minutes to go get to the next color change (grey toward green, green toward blue, and so on up to the golden finish), and high scores are no longer overwritten by an older score when the site is open in two tabs.

[v2.0.1]Bug-fix pass: the progress stripes no longer jerk at the end of each loop, the big total no longer overflows on very narrow phones, Mountain Climb no longer drifts toward an old tap position after a keyboard restart, the game switcher now announces its selected game correctly to screen readers, the hidden screen-reader total is rewritten only when it changes, and leftover flip-clock code was removed.

[v2.0]MEGA UPDATE 2: accent text and outlines now change color with the minutes left until the next milestone (grey, green, blue, then glowing red, purple and gold as it gets close); minigame high scores are saved on this device and update live during a run, so they are still there when you come back; and minigame fixes: no unfair death the instant Time Warp ends, Mountain Climb now keeps heading to where you tapped, and rocks no longer spawn in unavoidable clusters.

[v1.9.4]Added Mountain Climb as a second minigame in the same tab: climb the cliff with a live meter counter, dodge falling rocks (an amber marker warns where each one will land), and beat your best height. The progress card is a little shorter, and the first game no longer keeps drawing while it is hidden.

[v1.9.2]Flip clocks are gone: total minutes and the countdown units are now large, heavy, plain text that is easier to read at a glance.

[v1.9.1]Flip-clock numbers are bolder and bigger on higher-contrast cards, the countdown drops to three tiles per row on phones so nothing is cramped, the progress readout and panel headers wrap cleanly on narrow screens, the title and milestone details no longer redraw every tick, and Second Hand now ignores right-clicks and long-press menus.

[v1.9]Total minutes and the countdown now tick like a flip clock, the progress bar is easier to read, and Second Hand is sharper, pauses when out of view, and no longer drops your hold or restarts by accident, while the countdown stays exact across daylight-saving changes.

[v1.8]MEGA UPDATE: the page is now titled “Countdown To 7,000,000 Minutes!”, from 18th of July, 2013 at 12:30 PM NZT, and the milestone number updates itself as each milestone passes. The progress bar is now nearly twice as tall, in its own card, with animated stripes, a glowing leading edge, quarter markers, a larger percentage and a start, end and minutes-to-go scale underneath. This version label is now green for stable releases and red otherwise. Bug fixes: the countdown summary said “Under a minute to go” whenever less than an hour remained; the percentage could show 100.0000% before the milestone was actually reached; minigame obstacles popped into view at the start of each run; the orb could appear inside a wall on the start screen; and switching windows while holding left the orb stuck rising.

[v1.7]Made Second Hand much easier to control: the orb now climbs and falls at a steady rate instead of building up momentum, so short taps give small, precise nudges. The tunnel is wider with gentler bends, speed ramps up more slowly, each run starts centred in the tunnel with a short grace period against the walls, and the hitbox is a little smaller than the orb so near-misses count.

[v1.6]Added “Second Hand”, a collapsible one-button minigame: hold to rise through a winding tunnel, collect minutes, and trigger a slow-motion Time Warp every 5 minutes collected. Your best score is saved. Refreshed the look with new fonts (Plus Jakarta Sans and JetBrains Mono), a soft gradient backdrop and rounder panels.

[v1.5]The countdown panel and the update log can now be collapsed (your choice is remembered). Polished the countdown: all six units sit in one row, units that have already run out are dimmed, a plain-English summary sits under the numbers, and the panel turns amber in the final day. Fixed the clock skipping or repeating seconds, the countdown varying with the viewer’s time zone and daylight saving, the party banner sitting off-centre, and stale numbers after returning to a background tab.

[v1.4]Tracker is now live on the web. Repaired confetti library link and added a readout of the exact date and time the next milestone lands.

[v1.3]Added highly requested Update Log element to interface tracking patch adjustments.

[v1.2]Patched countdown system loop freeze. Shifted engine logic away from decimal math divisions to true calendar-rolling date components to dynamically counter freeze conditions under active ticks.

[v1.1]Expanded progress panel calculations with an absolute-value time countdown matrix rendering Years, Months, and Days smoothly.

[v1.0]Initial live deployment of 18 July 2013 NZT totalizer. Integrated active 1-minute full canvas confetti array.
